newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's air force repels "invaders" in wargames.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's air force repels "invaders" in wargames.

text.p: Algeria's combat planes, staging the largest mock air battle in years, cleared "invaders" from an imaginary occupied area in manoeuvres billed "1997 glory", state-run radio said on Wednesday.
Reconnaissance aircraft, bombers, fighters and helicopter-gunships took part in the three-day-long manoeuvres which ended on Tuesday, it said.
They were carried out in the barren area of Hassi Bahbah, some 200 km (120 miles) south of Algiers.
The usually sombre military chief of staff, Lieutenant-General Mohamed Lamari, was shown on state-run television broadly smiling as he briefed reporters on the exercises.
"Lamari expressed Algeria's pride in respect of the means deployed in the manoeuvres which displayed great operational capability," the radio said.
Lamari was quoted as saying that the wargames unfolded in "extremely difficult conditions" as the wind reached more than 140 km (90 miles) per hour at certain altitudes.

"The military wargames concluded with a clear-cut success. The fighters proved great mastery and an exceptional capability to defend the national territory," the official Algerian news agency APS said.
The military authorities, in a rare move of openness, invited foreign military attaches to witness the exercises, APS said.
It was Algeria's first large air force wargames since 1991.
